questions.q: A corneal ulcer is a discontinuity in the corneal epithelium plus cellular infiltration and ___ of the underlying layers.
questions.exp: Definition: discontinuity in corneal epithelium + cellular infiltration & necrosis of underlying layers. (Book p175)

questions.q: Which organism is the most common cause of bacterial corneal ulcer worldwide?
questions.exp: Etiology: Staphylococcus aureus: m/c worldwide. (Book p175)

questions.q: Which organism is the most common cause of bacterial corneal ulcer in India?
questions.exp: Pneumococcus: MC in India. (Book p175)

questions.q: A pneumococcal ulcer spreads from the centre to the periphery in a zigzag pattern and is accompanied by a hypopyon. What is this presentation called?
opts: Ulcer serpens with hypopyon corneal ulcer
Wreath shaped ulcer with pin head lesions
questions.exp: Pneumococcus: ulcer serpens - centre -> periphery in zigzag pattern; hypopyon corneal ulcer. (Book p175)

questions.q: A contact lens user develops a corneal ulcer with green discharge. Which organism does the book link to this?
questions.exp: Pseudomonas: m/c in contact lens users; green discharge. (Book p175)

questions.q: A corneal ulcer develops in a patient with a history of LASIK. Which group of organisms is m/c in this setting per the book?
questions.exp: Atypical mycobacteria: m/c in h/o LASIK. (Book p175)

questions.q: A wreath shaped or pin head ulcer is characteristic of ___.
questions.exp: Nocardia: wreath shaped/Pin head ulcer (photograph captioned Wreath shaped ulcer). (Book p175)

questions.q: In the pneumococcal ulcer photograph, the hypopyon is labelled as a collection of ___ in the anterior chamber.
questions.exp: Figure labels: Corneal ulcer; Hypopyon: Collection of pus in anterior chamber. (Book p175)

questions.q: Neisseria species (N. meningitidis and ___) are among the bacteria that can invade an intact epithelium.
questions.exp: Bacteria invading intact epithelium: Neisseria - N. meningitidis, N. gonorrhoea. (Book p175)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT in the book's list of bacteria invading intact epithelium?
questions.exp: The list: Neisseria, Corynebacterium diphtheria, Listeria, Shigella and Haemophilus aegyptius. Pseudomonas is listed separately as m/c in contact lens users. (Book p175)

questions.q: Along with Neisseria, Corynebacterium diphtheria, Listeria and Shigella, which organism completes the list of bacteria invading intact epithelium?
questions.exp: Last item of the list: Haemophilus aegyptius. (Book p175)

questions.q: An ulcer is saucer shaped with overhanging margins. Which pathogenic stage is this?
questions.exp: Stage 1 - Initial stage: Saucer shaped ulcer with overhanging margins. (Book p175)

questions.q: What characterises the progressive stage (stage 2) of a bacterial corneal ulcer?
opts: Smooth floor and edges with vascularization
Saucer shaped ulcer with overhanging margins
questions.exp: Stage 2 - Progressive stage: infiltration by PMNs; hypopyon; keratouveitis. (Book p175)

questions.q: In stage 2, the keratouveitis hypopyon is mobile, liquid like pus and is ___.
questions.exp: Keratouveitis: mobile - liquid like pus; sterile. (The fungal hypopyon is thick and immobile, p177.) (Book p175)

questions.q: Which stage diagrams are printed on p175, beside the pathogenesis text?
questions.exp: The diagram captions on p175 are Stage 1, Stage 2, Stage 3; Stage 4 is drawn on p176. (Book p175)

questions.q: An ulcer shows a smooth floor and edges, vascularization and a decreasing inflammatory response. Which stage is this?
questions.exp: Stage 3 - Regressive stage: smooth floor & edges of ulcer; vascularization +; decreased inflammatory response. (Book p176)

questions.q: Stage 4 (scar/cicatrization) of a corneal ulcer results in ___.
questions.exp: Stage 4 - Scar/Cicatrization: Permanent vision loss. (Book p176)

questions.q: Which pair describes an ectatic cicatrix?
opts: Herniation of Descemet's membrane through the ulcer
Thinning of the cornea, with bulging due to raised IOP (temporary/permanent)
Bulging with incarceration of iris tissue
Corneal surface formed by iris plugging a perforation
questions.exp: Ectatic cicatrix: thinning of cornea; bulging of cornea d/t raised IOP (temporary/permanent). (Book p176)

questions.q: The cornea bulges because of thinning together with incarceration of iris tissue. Which complication is this?
questions.exp: Anterior staphyloma: bulging of cornea d/t thinning + incarceration of iris tissue. (Book p176)

questions.q: Herniation of Descemet's membrane through a corneal ulcer is called a ___.
questions.exp: Descemetocoele: herniation of Descemet's membrane through corneal ulcer. (Book p176)

questions.q: After perforation of the cornea, the aqueous leak causes ___ IOP.
questions.exp: Perforation of cornea: a. Aqueous leak -> decreased IOP. (Book p176)

questions.q: After perforation, the corneal surface is re-formed by plugging of the perforation by iris tissue. What is this called?
questions.exp: Perforation: b. iris prolapse; c. pseudo-cornea - corneal surface formed d/t plugging of perforation by iris tissue. (Book p176)

questions.q: Which complication completes the list: ectatic cicatrix, anterior staphyloma, descemetocoele, perforation of cornea, and ___?
questions.exp: Complication 5: Endophthalmitis/Panophthalmitis. (Book p176)

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the captions under the four complication photographs on p176?
questions.exp: Captions: Lobulated Appearance of Anterior Staphyloma, Descemetocoele, Iris Prolapse, Pseudo-cornea. 'Ring abscess' is an Acanthamoeba figure (p177). (Book p176)

questions.q: When are antibiotics started in the book's management of bacterial corneal ulcer?
opts: Before any scraping is taken, on clinical grounds alone
Only after the stage 3 regressive phase
After gram staining and culture of the ulcer base scraping
questions.exp: MANAGEMENT - Antibiotics: after gram staining & culture of ulcer base, scraping. (Book p176)

questions.q: Match the fortified antibiotic with its strength — 1) Fortified Cephalozin  2) Fortified Tobramycin  … A) 1.3%  B) 5%  C) 0.15%  D) 0.02%
questions.exp: Fortified antibiotics: Fortified Cephalozin 5% + Fortified Tobramycin 1.3%. (Book p176)

questions.q: Atropine eye drops are given in bacterial corneal ulcer to:
questions.exp: Atropine eye drops: Relieve ciliary spasms. (Book p176)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed for impending perforation of the ulcer?
questions.exp: Impending perforation: oral doxycycline, soft bandage contact lens (BCL), cyanoacrylate glue. (Amphotericin B is for fungal ulcer, p177.) (Book p176)

questions.q: Steroids are contraindicated in bacterial corneal ulcer because of:
questions.exp: Contraindications: Steroids d/t epithelial thinning. (Book p176)

questions.q: The most common cause of fungal corneal ulcer is ___, a filamentous fungus with septate hyphae.
questions.exp: Fungal corneal ulcer m/c cause: Aspergillus (Filamentous fungi with septate hyphae). (Book p177)

questions.q: A patient develops a corneal ulcer after trauma with vegetative matter. Which infection does the book link to this history?
questions.exp: Fungal corneal ulcer: H/O trauma with vegetative fungi. (Book p177)

questions.q: True or false — 'In fungal corneal ulcer the symptoms are out of proportion to the signs.' Choose the correct verdict:
opts: True - symptoms are out of proportion to signs
False - signs and symptoms are always proportionate
True - the symptoms are out of proportion only in Acanthamoeba keratitis
False - the signs are out of proportion to the symptoms
questions.exp: Fungal ulcer signs: out of proportion to symptoms. (In Acanthamoeba keratitis it is symptoms out of proportion to signs, p177.) (Book p177)

questions.q: In the fungal corneal ulcer photograph, match the numbered arrows with the signs of the dry looking ulcer — 1) Arrow 1  2) Arrow 2  3) Arrow 3 (dashed arc)  … A) Satellite lesions  B) Wessely immune ring  C) Feathery ulcer margin
questions.exp: The dry looking ulcer signs are numbered 1. Feathery ulcer margin, 2. Satellite lesions, 3. Wessely Immune Ring, matching the arrow numbers in the Fungal Corneal Ulcer photograph. (Book p177)

questions.q: The Wessely immune ring of fungal ulcer consists of ___.
opts: Collection of pus in anterior chamber
Inflammation of nerves throughout the cornea
questions.exp: 3. Wessely Immune Ring: Antigen-antibody complexes. (Book p177)

questions.q: Which description fits the hypopyon of a fungal corneal ulcer in the book?
opts: Mobile, liquid like pus and sterile
Mobile, liquid like pus and written as 'Asterile'
questions.exp: Fungal ulcer hypopyon: thick, immobile, 'Asterile'. (The bacterial keratouveitis hypopyon is mobile, liquid like pus, sterile - p175.) (Book p177)

questions.q: Which drug is the DOC (drug of choice) for Aspergillus fusarium keratitis in the book?
questions.exp: Natamycin 5% eye drops: DOC for Aspergillus fusarium. (Book p177)

questions.q: What strength of amphotericin B eye drops is listed for fungal corneal ulcer?
questions.exp: Amphotericin B 0.15% eye drops. (Book p177)

questions.q: In fungal corneal ulcer, atropine is a supportive treatment. What is the book's statement on steroids?
opts: Steroids are the drug of choice
Steroids are given with natamycin only after 2 weeks
questions.exp: Atropine: supportive Rx. Steroids: C/I. (Book p177)

questions.q: A contact lens user with contaminated solution, who washes lenses in tap water and swims in pools, develops keratitis. Which infection does the book list?
questions.exp: Acanthamoeba risk factors: unhygienic practices in contact lens users - contaminated solution, washing in tap water, swimming pools. (Book p177)

questions.q: Which statement about clinical features of Acanthamoeba keratitis matches the book?
opts: Symptoms are out of proportion to signs
Signs are out of proportion to symptoms
There are no symptoms until perforation
questions.exp: Acanthamoeba clinical features: symptoms out of proportion to signs (opposite of fungal ulcer, whose signs are out of proportion to symptoms). (Book p177)

questions.q: Pseudodendritic keratitis is listed among the signs of which infection in the book's Acanthamoeba section?
questions.exp: Acanthamoeba signs: pseudodendritic keratitis, radial keratoneuritis, ring shaped ulcer with abscess. (Book p177)

questions.q: Radial keratoneuritis is inflammation of ___ throughout the cornea.
questions.exp: Radial keratoneuritis: inflammation of nerves throughout cornea. (Book p177)

questions.q: A ring shaped ulcer with abscess (figure: Ring abscess) is described by the book as ___ of Acanthamoeba keratitis.
questions.exp: Ring shaped ulcer with abscess: Pathognomonic. (Book p177)

questions.q: In the gram staining picture for Acanthamoeba, the arrow label reads:
questions.exp: Investigation 1. Gram staining - label: Double walled Acanthamoeba cyst. (Book p177)

questions.q: Which culture medium does the book give for Acanthamoeba?
opts: Non-nutrient agar enriched with E. coli
questions.exp: Investigation 2. Culture media: Non-nutrient agar enriched with E. coli. (Book p177)

questions.q: Among the drugs inhibiting membrane synthesis for Acanthamoeba keratitis, which is the DOC?
questions.exp: Drugs inhibiting membrane synthesis: PHMB 0.02% (Polyhexamethylene biguanide): DOC. (Book p178)

questions.q: Besides PHMB, which other membrane synthesis inhibitor is listed, and at what strength?
questions.exp: Drugs inhibiting membrane synthesis: PHMB 0.02% (DOC) and Chlorhexidine 0.02%. (Book p178)

questions.q: The most commonly used drug inhibiting DNA synthesis in Acanthamoeba keratitis is ___.
questions.exp: Drugs inhibiting DNA synthesis: Propamidine: m/c. (Book p178)

questions.q: Match the HSV infection with its presentation — 1) Primary (1°) infection  2) Recurrent infection  … A) Keratitis  B) Conjunctivitis  C) Disciform keratitis
questions.exp: HSV: 1° infection: conjunctivitis; recurrent infection: keratitis. (Book p178)

questions.q: HSV epithelial lesions of keratitis are due to:
questions.exp: Clinical features a. Epithelial lesions: d/t active viral replication (seen with fluorescence staining). (Book p178)

questions.q: In the fluorescence staining pictures of HSV epithelial lesions, the progression drawn by arrows is:
opts: Geographic ulcer, then dendritic ulcer, then superficial punctate keratitis
Dendritic ulcer, then superficial punctate keratitis, then geographic ulcer
Superficial punctate keratitis, then geographic ulcer, then dendritic ulcer
Superficial punctate (dot like) keratitis, then dendritic ulcer (branching with terminal buds), then geographic ulcer
questions.exp: Figure sequence with arrows: Superficial punctate (Dot like) keratitis -> Dendritic ulcer: Branching with terminal buds -> Geographic ulcer. (Book p178)

questions.q: What is the book's treatment for HSV epithelial keratitis?
opts: 3% acyclovir eye ointment 5 times/day for 10-14 days, plus topical steroids
Oral acyclovir 800 mg 5 times/day for 2 weeks, with steroids contraindicated
3% acyclovir eye ointment 5 times/day for 10-14 days, with steroids contraindicated
questions.exp: Rx: 3% acyclovir eye ointment: 5 times/day x 10-14 days. Steroids: C/I. (Book p178)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as another differential diagnosis for dendritic ulcer?
questions.exp: Other d/d's for dendritic ulcer: Acanthamoeba keratitis, HZV keratitis, tyrosinemia, contact lens overuse. (Book p178)

questions.q: Immune stromal keratitis is due to type ___ hypersensitivity.
questions.exp: Immune stromal keratitis: d/t type III hypersensitivity. (Disciform keratitis is type IV, p179.) (Book p178)

questions.q: Immune stromal keratitis occurs following which lesion, and how does the book treat it?
opts: Following disciform keratitis; 3% acyclovir ointment alone
Following necrotizing stromal keratitis; steroids contraindicated
Following epithelial keratitis; 3% acyclovir ointment with steroids contraindicated
Following epithelial keratitis; 3% acyclovir ointment + topical steroids
questions.exp: Immune stromal keratitis occurs following epithelial keratitis. Rx: 3% Acyclovir ointment + Topical steroids. (Book p178)

questions.q: Which is the most severe form of HSV stromal keratitis in the book, and how is it treated?
opts: Immune stromal keratitis; 3% acyclovir ointment + topical steroids
Necrotizing stromal keratitis; 3% acyclovir ointment + topical steroids
questions.exp: Necrotizing stromal keratitis: most severe form of stromal keratitis. Rx: 3% Acyclovir ointment + Topical steroids. (Book p178)

questions.q: In the photograph captioned 'Immune Stromal Keratitis', the arrow label reads:
questions.exp: Figure caption: Immune Stromal Keratitis - label: Central stromal haze. (Book p178)

questions.q: An HSV endothelial lesion shows disc shaped areas of deep stromal/endothelial edema. What is it called?
questions.exp: c. Endothelial lesion: i. Disciform keratitis: disc shaped areas of deep stromal/endothelial edema. (Book p179)

questions.q: Disciform keratitis is a type ___ hypersensitivity reaction.
questions.exp: Disciform keratitis: Type IV hypersensitivity reaction. (Immune stromal keratitis is type III, p178.) (Book p179)

questions.q: A patient with HSV keratitis has corneal anaesthesia followed by a neurotrophic ulcer. What is this called and what is the cause?
opts: Metaherpetic keratitis, due to 3rd cranial nerve palsy
Disciform keratitis, due to 5th cranial nerve palsy
Metaherpetic keratitis, due to 5th cranial nerve palsy
Sclerokeratitis, due to 3rd cranial nerve palsy
questions.exp: Hallmark of HSV keratitis: Corneal anaesthesia -> Metaherpetic keratitis/Neurotrophic ulcer d/t 5th Cranial Nerve palsy. (Book p179)

questions.q: Herpes zoster ophthalmicus affects the dermatome supplied by the ophthalmic branch of the ___ cranial nerve.
questions.exp: HERPES ZOSTER OPHTHALMICUS/SHINGLES: affects dermatome supplied by ophthalmic branch of 5th cranial nerve. (Book p179)

questions.q: A patient with shingles has a rash involving the tip of the nose. What does Hutchinson's sign indicate?
opts: A decreased chance of Herpes zoster ophthalmicus
An increased chance of Herpes zoster ophthalmicus
questions.exp: Hutchinson's sign: rash involving tip of the nose -> increased chance of Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus. (Book p179)

questions.q: True or false — 'The pseudodendritic ulcer of HZO has a branching pattern with terminal buds.' Choose the correct verdict:
opts: True - terminal buds are the hallmark of the pseudodendritic ulcer
False - it has terminal buds only in chronic cases
False - the pseudodendritic ulcer branches with no terminal buds
True - terminal buds appear only in the geographic stage
questions.exp: HZO clinical feature 1: Pseudodendritic ulcer - branching pattern with no terminal buds. (HSV dendritic ulcer: branching with terminal buds, p178.) (Book p179)

questions.q: A patient with herpes zoster has keratitis with coin shaped sub-epithelial lesions. Which HZO feature is this?
questions.exp: HZO clinical feature 2: Nummular keratitis (figure label: coin shaped sub-epithelial lesions). (Book p179)

questions.q: Which HZO feature is seen in chronic cases, and which feature follows it in the book's list?
opts: Nummular keratitis; then mucous plaque keratitis
Stromal keratitis; then cranial nerve palsy
Mucous plaque keratitis; then stromal keratitis
questions.exp: 3. Mucous plaque keratitis: in chronic cases; 4. Stromal keratitis. (Book p179)

questions.q: Which cranial nerve palsy is the most common in HZO per the book?
questions.exp: 5. Cranial nerve palsy: 3rd cranial nerve - m/c. (Book p179)

questions.q: Which HZO finding is the least common?
questions.exp: 6. Sclerokeratitis: Least common finding. (Book p179)

questions.q: Post-herpetic neuralgia is defined as persistence of pain after how long of resolution?
questions.exp: 7. Post-herpetic neuralgia: Persistence of pain after 1 month of resolution. (Book p179)

questions.q: Post-herpetic neuralgia pain is worse at which time?
questions.exp: Post-herpetic neuralgia: worse at night. (Book p179)

questions.q: What is the book's oral treatment for herpes zoster ophthalmicus?
opts: T. Acyclovir 400 mg x 3 times/day x 10 days
T. Acyclovir 800 mg x 5 times/day x 2 weeks
3% acyclovir eye ointment 5 times/day x 10-14 days
T. Acyclovir 800 mg x 2 times/day x 1 week
questions.exp: Treatment: T. Acyclovir 800 mg x 5 times/day x 2 weeks. (Book p179)

questions.q: The facial photograph of a crusted rash over the forehead and lids is captioned ___, and the second photograph's label reads 'coin shaped sub-epithelial lesions' under ___.
questions.exp: Figure captions on p179: Shingles; Nummular keratitis (label: coin shaped sub-epithelial lesions). (Book p179)
